title: “Rāhula, develop the meditation on foulness. Rāhula, by developing the meditation on foulness, what is called lust is abandoned. Rāhula, develop the meditation on impermanence.…
content: “Rāhula, develop the meditation on foulness. Rāhula, by developing the meditation on foulness, what is called lust is abandoned. Rāhula, develop the meditation on impermanence. Rāhula, by developing the meditation on impermanence, what is called the conceit ‘I am’ is abandoned.”

title: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering;…
content: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering; perception is suffering; formations are suffering; consciousness is suffering. This, monks, is called suffering. And what, monks, is the root of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting here and there — that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence.”

title: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of feelings? Feelings are impermanent, suffering, subject to change – that is the peril in the…
content: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of feelings? Feelings are impermanent, suffering, subject to change – that is the peril in the case of feelings. And what, monks, is the escape in the case of feelings? The removal of desire and lust for feelings, the abandoning of desire and lust – that is the escape in the case of feelings.”

title: “And how, householder, is wandering without a home? Regarding the form element, householder, whatever there is of desire, lust, delight, craving, any engagement and clinging,…
content: “And how, householder, is wandering without a home? Regarding the form element, householder, whatever there is of desire, lust, delight, craving, any engagement and clinging, mental standpoints, attachments, underlying tendencies — the Tathāgata has abandoned them, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, made them non-existent, so that they cannot arise again in the future. Therefore, the Tathāgata is called ‘one who wanders without a home.’ Regarding the feeling element … perception element … formation element … consciousness element — the Tathāgata has abandoned them … Therefore, the Tathāgata is called ‘one who wanders without a home.’”

title: “Monks, what is Right Effort? Monks, here a monk awakens desire for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy,…
content: “Monks, what is Right Effort? Monks, here a monk awakens desire for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives. He awakens desire for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives. He awakens desire for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives. He awakens desire for the continuance, non-disappearance, strengthening, increase, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives. This, monks, is called Right Effort.”

title: “And for what benefit, monks, should a monk dwell with the perception of disgust toward the non-disgusting? ‘May greed not arise in me toward agreeable…
content: “And for what benefit, monks, should a monk dwell with the perception of disgust toward the non-disgusting? ‘May greed not arise in me toward agreeable states.’ For this benefit, monks, a monk should dwell with the perception of disgust toward the non-disgusting. And for what benefit, monks, should a monk dwell with the perception of non-disgust toward the disgusting? ‘May hatred not arise in me toward states that provoke hatred.’ For this benefit, a monk should dwell with the perception of non-disgust toward the disgusting. And for what benefit should a monk, abandoning both the non-disgusting and the disgusting, dwell equanimously, mindful and clearly comprehending? ‘May greed not arise in me toward agreeable states, wherever, however; may hatred not arise in me toward states that provoke hatred, wherever, however; may delusion not arise in me toward states that provoke delusion, wherever, however.’ For this benefit, monks, a monk, abandoning both the non-disgusting and the disgusting, dwells equanimously, mindful and clearly comprehending.”

title: “Monks, suppose there is a bronze cup of drinking water that has color, smell, and taste, and that drinking water is mixed with poison. Then…
content: “Monks, suppose there is a bronze cup of drinking water that has color, smell, and taste, and that drinking water is mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. Someone says to him: ‘Good man, this bronze cup of drinking water has color, smell, and taste, and it is mixed with poison. If you wish, drink it. While drinking, you will delight in its color, smell, and taste. After drinking, you may meet death or deadly suffering.’ That man might drink it without reflection, without refusal. While drinking, he delights in its color, smell, and taste. After drinking, he meets death or deadly suffering. Monks, I say that this course of practice is like that simile — namely, a course of practice that is pleasant in the present but has painful results in the future.”

title: Those who are intoxicated with states, Bewildered and confused, Led astray into wrong courses, Wandering amidst various views — They sleep on and on, They…
content:
Those who are intoxicated with states,
Bewildered and confused,
Led astray into wrong courses,
Wandering amidst various views —
They sleep on and on,
They do not wake up.
Now indeed the time has come
For them to awaken.

(The Blessed One):
Those who are not intoxicated with states,
Not bewildered or confused,
Not led astray into wrong courses,
Wandering amidst various views —
They have attained perfect enlightenment,
They have fully understood.
On the uneven path,
They walk evenly.

title: Elder Nitaka: The mind is like a rock, Standing firm, unmoved. Toward agreeable things, The mind has no desire. Toward things that disturb, The mind…
content:
Elder Nitaka:

The mind is like a rock,
Standing firm, unmoved.
Toward agreeable things,
The mind has no desire.
Toward things that disturb,
The mind is not disturbed.
One whose mind is thus developed —
From where can suffering come?

My mind is like a rock,
Standing firm, unmoved.
Toward agreeable things,
My mind has no desire.
Toward things that disturb,
My mind is not disturbed.
My mind is thus developed —
From where can suffering come to me?

title: “Monks, suppose there is urine mixed with various medicines. Then a person with jaundice comes, and someone says to him: ‘Good man, this urine is…
content: “Monks, suppose there is urine mixed with various medicines. Then a person with jaundice comes, and someone says to him: ‘Good man, this urine is mixed with various medicines. If you wish, drink it. While drinking, you will not delight in its color, smell, or taste. But after drinking, you will be at ease.’ That person might drink it after reflection, without refusal. While drinking, he does not delight in its color, smell, or taste. But after drinking, he is at ease. Monks, I say that this course of practice is like that simile — namely, a course of practice that is painful in the present but has pleasant results in the future.”
